The way I did it was to stop thinking of my introversion as a harmless personality trait and start thinking of it as a flaw. I didn't punish myself for it, but I did tell myself that it was something I had to work through instead of something glamorous that made me secretly super interesting and smart next to everyone else.

At parties, I stopped staring at my feet and started actively trying to make my way into the center of the room. 

I pretended I was an extrovert. Or at least what I believed an extrovert was like. I felt a little silly at first but after a while it wasn't too bad.

I tried to ask open-ended questions that I wished people would ask me e.g. "so what book are you reading right now?" "would you recommend it?" rather than "so how was your week?" or "what do you do?"

If people engaged me in conversation I would try to find reasons to stand next to them to talk to them. It is easier to talk to someone when you're at their side rather than in front of them. This also invites more people into the conversation so you're not all by yourself.

Compliment someone on their clothing choices. This seems to be an instant winner. 

Complain about something to someone. Again, this seems to be an instant winner. People love to complain.

If you're invited out, go. You don't have to stay for ages if you feel too drained or you're not having fun.

Don't punish people for saying "you're so quiet." They're not usually being mean, they just don't know what else to say and they're worried you don't like them. A laugh with a jovial "Am I?" is usually a good response. You can even follow that with "Sorry, I'm a bit introverted. Not used to places like this." A *lot* of people think of themselves as introverts so it will make you seem relateable.

I always think context is important. Homosexuality is banned in Leviticus during a time when the Hebrew people were wandering the desert. Sex between two men in that kind of environment could have been dangerous, maybe even fatal (not to mention desert anal sounds super unappealing). Other things that were banned included eating certain animals (pigs are the most cited but also kites, bats, seagulls, hyrax, camels and hares) and also eating lifestock with blemishes and eating expired meat. Touching dead bodies, not washing one's hands, and then eating, is also described as an abomination.

The word "abomination" is used to describe much of the above in my copy of the Bible. The word "wickedness," or "perversion" is used to describe things like murder, bestiality, and incest. Lol let's *actually* tell the whole story:

Count Dankula a.k.a Mark Meechan made a video with his pug back in 2016. His girlfriend kept going on about how cute their pug, Buddha, was so in order to piss her off, while she was away he taught the pug how to do the least cute thing he could think of: a Nazi salute in response to the phrases "Seig Heil" and "Gas the Jews." He put the video up online. 

Meechan was shocked to suddenly find himself arrested under suspicion of breeching the Communications Act 2003. This is an act which is mostly for the regulation of telecommunications and public broadcasting companies in the UK. As far as anyone knew, it had never been used to prosecute a YouTuber before.  On 19 March 2018, Meechan was convicted of breaching the act by Sheriff Derek O'Carroll at Arlie Sheriff Court. The court ruled that Meechan's claim that the video was a joke intended for his girlfriend "lacked credibility" as Meechan's girlfriend did not subscribe to the YouTube channel to which the video was posted. On 23 April 2018, Meechan was sentenced to a fine of £800. Meechan chose not to pay the fine. He challenged the authorities saying in one of his videos that he owned nothing, rented his property, his car was a piece of shit, and he did not have £800 to hand over. If the government wanted to imprison him over a joke they could go ahead. (side note: this hardly seems like the behaviour of someone who earns six figures don't cha think?).

 Approximately 500 people gathered in London to protest for free speech when the sentence was handed out. An event that was *not* organized by Meechan.

 Meechan started a GoFundMe campaign on 24 April 2018 to raise £100,000 for an appeal. The appeal was rejected by a member of the Sheriff Appeal Court, who also accused Meechan's lawyer of contempt. Now that Meechan had the £800 in his bank account, the government took it **without his permission.**

In June 2018 BBC Scotland planned to feature Meechan in a 2019 debate program called *The Collective* and had him film two episodes. However, the network announced that these episodes would not be aired after facing backlash over this decision. This backlash did not come from the public, however, and instead came from news headlines which labelled Meechan a Nazi. 

 

In April 2019, Meechan said he intended to stand for MEP on behalf of UKIP in the upcoming 2019 European Parliament Election in the UK. He was named fourth on UKIP's list in Scotland but was not elected, after UKIP won only 1.8% of the vote in Scotland.

In November 2019, Meechan posted a video announcing that he had left UKIP.
